study_identification_part.si4_title: Analyzing heterogeneity in Alzheimer disease using multimodal normative modeling on imaging-based ATN biomarkers

study_characteristics_part.sc1_study_objective: To identify individual patterns of neuroanatomical and neuropathological variation in individuals with Alzheimer disease using deep learning-based normative modeling across amyloid-tau-neurodegeneration (ATN) imaging biomarker data, and to develop a disease severity index that captures both spatial extent and magnitude of regional abnormal deviations.

caa6_deviation_metric.answer: Z-score based on reconstruction error from mmVAE; Binary abnormality thresholding: |Z| ≥ 1.96 (Z < -1.96 for MRI atrophy; Z > 1.96 for amyloid and tau burden); Disease Severity Index (DSI): inner product of binary abnormality map and regional deviation vector, normalized by total number of regions
caa6_deviation_metric.reason: The study used multiple deviation metrics: (1) Individual-level Z-scores calculated by normalizing reconstruction errors from the mmVAE using mean and variance from the holdout validation set; (2) Binary abnormality maps identifying regions with statistically significant deviations (Z < -1.96 for MRI indicating atrophy, Z > 1.96 for amyloid/tau indicating pathological accumulation, corresponding to bottom/top 2.5% of normative distribution); (3) Disease Severity Index (DSI) combining spatial extent and magnitude of abnormal deviations.
caa6_deviation_metric.supporting_text: For each participant in ADNI-ADS and ADRC-ADS, deviations for each region and for each modality can be calculated as the squared error between input and reconstructed data ... We utilized the mean and variance (calculated independently for each region) from ADNI-CU-holdout to normalize regional deviations in the ADNI-ADS cohort across each modality ... This step generated regional, modality-specific Z-score deviations for each individual in the ADS cohort relative to the normative range of the respective reference control group. ... For MRI gray matter volumes, regional Z-scores below -1.96 (bottom 2.5% of the normative distribution) were labeled as abnormal (statistically significant) deviations ... Similarly regional deviations in amyloid-FBP and tau-FTP SUVR were identified as abnormal if their Z-scores were above 1.96 (top 2.5% of the normative distribution). ... DSI was calculated separately for each modality (DSI_mri, DSI_amyloid, DSI_tau) and also aggregated across all modalities (DSI_all). Specifically, every individual's DSI was calculated by (i) first performing an inner product between the binary thresholded abnormality map and the regional deviation vector; and (ii) then normalizing the inner product by the total number of regions

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa7_association_analysis: Linear regression (age and sex adjusted) to test associations between DSI measures (DSI_all, DSI_mri, DSI_amyloid, DSI_tau) and neuropsychological composites (memory, executive functioning, language); Pearson correlation coefficients; Steiger's Z-test to compare correlations between DSI measures and classical ATN biomarkers (hippocampal volume, amyloid Centiloid, tau index); ANOVA and Tukey post-hoc tests (FDR-corrected) for group comparisons of DSI across CDR stages; Cohen's d effect sizes for regional pairwise group differences; Mann-Whitney U tests for comparing classical biomarkers between cohorts; Hamming distance to quantify dissimilarity in binary abnormality maps between individuals; median hamming distance comparisons across groups with Tukey post-hoc tests; Kaplan-Meier survival analysis for CDR progression with log-rank tests (FDR-corrected) comparing DSI quantiles
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa8_key_findings_brief: The study demonstrated heterogeneous patterns of abnormal deviations in regional gray matter, amyloid, and tau between AD patients, with higher within-group heterogeneity at more severe dementia stages; a multimodal disease severity index (DSI_all) was associated with cognitive impairment and increased risk of disease progression.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa9_key_findings_detailed: The study found evidence of substantial heterogeneity in Alzheimer disease using multimodal normative modeling. Regional abnormal deviations showed distinct spatial patterns: highest proportion in hippocampal regions for MRI atrophy (47% in CDR≥1), precuneus and frontal regions for amyloid burden (100% in CDR≥1), and hippocampal/entorhinal regions for tau deposition (84% in CDR≥1). Within-group heterogeneity, measured by Hamming distance, was significantly higher at progressive dementia stages, with median hamming_all of 62 (IQR 39) for CDR≥1, 56 (IQR 34) for CDR=0.5, and 47 (IQR 30) for CDR=0 in ADNI-ADS. MRI showed the highest spatial heterogeneity, followed by tau and amyloid. The developed DSI_all metric increased with dementia severity (ADNI-ADS: mean 1.8 for CDR≥1, 1.1 for CDR=0.5, 0.45 for CDR=0, 0.06 for CU). DSI_all was significantly associated with all cognitive domains in both cohorts (ADNI-ADS: memory r=-0.62, executive r=-0.54, language r=-0.47; ADRC-ADS: memory r=-0.68, executive r=-0.56, language r=-0.41, all p<0.001). Higher DSI_all quartiles (q3 and q4) were associated with significantly increased risk of progression to CDR≥1 compared to lower quartiles (p<0.01). All findings were replicated in the independent Knight ADRC cohort, demonstrating generalizability.

caa10_key_limitations.answer: Cross-sectional design limiting ability to distinguish disease stages from subtypes; demographic differences between ADNI and ADRC cohorts affecting generalizability; limited to North American populations; different FreeSurfer versions and scanners between cohorts introducing variability; lack of cerebrovascular disease burden measurements
caa10_key_limitations.supporting_text: First, we used cross-sectional imaging data for our normative modeling framework, providing a snapshot of the disease at a specific time. Due to the cross-sectional setting, it is challenging to distinguish between stages and subtypes. ... Demographic differences between the ADNI and Knight ADRC cohorts, such as age and sex distributions, present a limitation in our study. ... Additionally, both ADNI and Knight ADRC datasets consisted of individuals from North America only, which are not representative of the general population. ... Third, the imaging scans in the discovery and replication cohorts were processed with different versions of FreeSurfer (FreeSurfer 6 for ADNI and FreeSurfer 5.3 for ADRC), and the imaging data were acquired using different MRI scanners. ... Finally, cerebrovascular disease burden is an important co-pathology in AD, contributing to cognitive decline independently or synergistically with amyloid and tau pathologies. While our study focused on neurodegeneration as a key co-pathology to study deviations in brain structure, we acknowledge that vascular burden represents an essential dimension to understand AD.

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa11_application_notes: The study stratified participants by CDR scores rather than traditional diagnostic categories; used Hamming distance to quantify inter-individual heterogeneity in spatial patterns; developed case studies with KDE plots and heatmaps to visualize subgroups within clinical cohorts; DSI metric designed to be potentially useful for monitoring patient response to FDA-approved anti-amyloid treatments (aducanumab, lecanemab); conducted sensitivity analyses comparing DSI measures to classical ATN biomarkers using Steiger's Z-test

general_note_part.gn1_general_notes: This study used a deep learning-based multimodal variational autoencoder (mmVAE) framework to perform normative modeling across three imaging modalities (T1-weighted MRI, amyloid PET, tau PET) representing the ATN framework. The model was trained on ADNI data (N=326 training; N=434 total controls) and validated on an independent Knight ADRC cohort (N=301 controls) using transfer learning. Only Florbetapir tracer data were included to avoid harmonization issues. The framework used a Product-of-Experts (POE) approach to learn a shared latent space across modalities. Model hyperparameters: epochs=500, learning rate=10^-5, batch size=256, latent dimension=64, 4 fully-connected layers (512-256-128-64) in encoder and decoder. Age was one-hot encoded for 47-91 years (44 positions) and sex as binary (2 positions). Both were concatenated with latent code in decoders. The study found that DSI_all values differed between ADNI and ADRC cohorts (higher in ADNI), likely reflecting higher overall pathology in ADNI due to its focus on later disease stages versus ADRC's focus on preclinical phases. Comparison of classical biomarkers confirmed higher hippocampal atrophy and tau burden in ADNI even within similar CDR groups (p<0.05). Code will be made publicly available upon acceptance. Visualization used Python package ggseg for brain atlases and KDE plots for distribution analysis.
